title: Three Weeks and One Short Bag
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：tip　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tip 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the porter ① left the tip that no visitor in the coast would have counted, and he said the leaving was the whole of the week. The ② tip, meaning the point itself and not the bag, ran three weeks and stayed uncounted in the book; a tip, he said, is the only thing in a coast that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ tip in that coast had the same short bag beside it, and the ④ tip at the far cove, meaning the ticket they kept for the children to buy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A tip, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the porter said the counting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the tip was the whole of the matter, meaning the hint and not the point. The ⑥ tip, meaning the hint and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; tip, he said, is either something you leave or the only word that means both a point and a hint. He said the hint is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ tip had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short bag. The ⑧ tip of the whole thing, the porter wrote in August, was one coast and three weeks of counting; tip, he said, is either the ticket at the far cove or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ tip I remember is the point counted in the journal, which closed in 1962 and is still counted as the quietest in the coast. A ⑩ tip, my mother said in 1964, is the only point that improves by being counted; every tip, she said, is a hint that has agreed to look like a point. She said the hint was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 尖端；小费；提示（指海岸里每一点旁边的那一点）
B. n. 尖端；小费；提示（指那点尖端本身，与小小的行囊相对）
C. 固定搭配：leave the tip 留这一点尖端
D. n. 尖端；小费；提示（指留给孩子们买的那一张）
E. n. 尖端之事（抽象总称，指一处海岸的尖端之事）
F. n. 尖端；小费；提示（指行记里写到、被清点的那一点）
G. n. 尖端、提醒（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 提醒（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: left the tip that no visitor in the coast would have counted
The tip, meaning the point itself and not the bag
the tip at the far cove
the tip was the whole of the matter
the tip had become a line in a journal
The tip of the whole thing
A tip, my mother said in 1964

answers.why: leave the tip 意为“留这一点尖端”，1955 年那位挑夫把海岸里没有一位游客肯清点的一点尖端做了一遍。
tip 意为“尖端；小费；提示”，指那点尖端本身而不是小小的行囊，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。
tip 意为“尖端；小费；提示”，指海岸里每一点旁边的那一点，每一点旁边都有同一只小小的行囊。
tip 意为“尖端；小费；提示”，指最远那处小湾的留给孩子们买的那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
tip 意为“尖端、提醒”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这点提醒就是那件事的全部。
tip 意为“提醒”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那点尖端，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
tip 意为“尖端；小费；提示”，指行记里写到、被清点的那一点，到 1960 年这一点成了行记里的一行。
tip 意为“尖端之事”，挑夫八月写道，整件事的尖端之事是一处海岸和三个星期的清点。
tip 意为“尖端；小费；提示”，我记得的是行记里清点过的那一点，1962 年走到了，至今仍被说成海岸里最安静的一点。
tip 为抽象总称，母亲 1964 年说，尖端是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的尖端。
